## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

Confluence's "Development Standards" (261750785) and "Component Override Strategy" (261881857) — see [[reference-confluence-sfcc-space]] — contradict current repo rules in two places:

Confluence's "Technical Environment Setup" (304906242) still describes a flat `cp .env.sample .env` setup with no mention of the tiered `.env.shared`/`.env.<tier>` system or `scripts/switchEnv.mjs` — almost certainly stale, since `feature/env-switching` (the branch that built that tooling) was still active as of 2026-07-15.

**How to apply:** when Confluence and the repo disagree, trust the repo (AGENTS.md/.claude/rules) as source of truth for code conventions, but flag the Confluence page as needing an update per AGENTS.md's doc-integrity rule rather than silently ignoring the mismatch — especially once `feature/env-switching` merges, since 304906242 will then be actively wrong for new hires.

      "value": "This page documents the alternative catalogue sync design using **SCAPI Admin APIs** instead of WebDAV file-based import. It covers the same three data domains — Product, Price, and Inventory — and follows the same section structure as the file-based design for direct comparison.

> **Context:** The file-based design (WebDAV + import job) is the recommended approach for Zimmermann's catalogue scale. This SCAPI Admin API design is documented as the alternative pattern — applicable for real-time single-product event scenarios or if the file-based approach is ruled out. See the [parent page comparison](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/312508418) for the full pro/con trade-off.

Related pages: - [TSD: Catalogue Sync — Product, Price & Inventory (MuleSoft → SFCC)](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/312508418) — file-based design - [TSD: Product — SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/292061208) - [TSD: Product — SFCC Product Attributes](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/312377345) - [TSD: Price — SFCC Pricebooks & Global-e](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/292388871)

---

1-overview1. Overview
---------------------

In the SCAPI Admin API pattern, MuleSoft calls SFCC REST endpoints directly per product or inventory record. Each domain uses a dedicated SCAPI Admin API family.

> **API Note:** OCAPI is deprecated. All SFCC Admin API calls use **SCAPI Admin APIs** authenticated via **Account Manager OAuth2 (AmOAuth2)** — client credentials grant.
>
> ⚠️ **Price sync exception:** There is no published SCAPI Admin API or verified OCAPI endpoint for writing pricebook entries programmatically. **Price sync must always use the file-based pricebook XML import** (WebDAV + `sfcc-site-archive-import` job) regardless of which pattern is chosen for products and inventory. See Section 5.

| Domain | Mechanism | SCAPI API | Auth | API Reference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Product | SCAPI Admin API (per product/variant) | Products Admin API — `POST` / `PUT` | AmOAuth2 | [Products](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/commerce-api/references/products) |
| Price | **File-based only** — WebDAV + import job | No SCAPI API exists | AmOAuth2 (WebDAV) | — |
| Inventory | SCAPI Admin API (per record) | Inventory Lists API — `PUT` / `PATCH` | AmOAuth2 | [Inventory Lists](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/commerce-api/references/inventory-lists) |

**SCAPI Admin API base URL:**Defaultnonehttps://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com

**Auth token acquisition (product and inventory domains):**DefaultnonePOST https://account.demandware.com/dwsso/oauth2/access\_token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
grant\_type=client\_credentials
&client\_id={mulesoftClientId}
&client\_secret={mulesoftClientSecret}

---

2-sequencing-constraints2. Sequencing Constraints
-------------------------------------------------

Unlike the file-based import job which handles sequencing internally, the SCAPI Admin API pattern requires MuleSoft to enforce strict operation order across product and inventory domains. Price sync runs independently via file-based import and does not participate in this sequence.

DefaultnoneFor each style (master product):
STEP 1 — Create or update MASTER product
POST /product/v1/.../products/{catalogId}
STEP 2 — Create or update each VARIANT
POST /product/v1/.../products/{catalogId}
⚠ Must complete after Step 1 — variant fails if master does not exist
STEP 3 — Assign products to CATEGORIES
PUT /product/v1/.../categories/{categoryId}/products/{productId}
⚠ Must complete after Step 1
STEP 4 — Write INVENTORY
PUT /inventory/v1/.../inventory-lists/{listId}/product-inventory-records/{productId}
⚠ Must complete after Step 2 — variant must exist before inventory record
STEP 5 — PRICE SYNC (file-based — independent of above sequence)
Pricebook XML → WebDAV → sfcc-site-archive-import job
Runs on its own schedule
⚠ Variant must exist in SFCC before a pricebook entry for it is valid

---

3-sync-orchestration--mulesoft-flow-product-and-inventory3. Sync Orchestration — MuleSoft Flow (Product and Inventory)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The SCAPI Admin API pattern requires a **separate MuleSoft flow per domain** (product, inventory), each with its own retry logic, error tracking, and partial-success handling. Price sync uses the file-based flow documented in the [parent page](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/312508418).

DefaultnoneAP21 / NewStore (source event or scheduler trigger)
│
▼
MuleSoft
│
├── 1. GET AmOAuth2 TOKEN
│ POST https://account.demandware.com/dwsso/oauth2/access\_token
│ Cache token; refresh before expiry (typically 30 min TTL)
│
├── 2. CHECK PRODUCT EXISTS (product domain only)
│ GET /product/v1/.../products/{catalogId}/{productId}
│ → 200: product exists → use PUT to update
│ → 404: product does not exist → use POST to create
│
├── 3. EXECUTE API CALL
│ POST / PUT per domain (see Sections 4 and 6)
│ Headers: Authorization: Bearer {amOAuth2Token}
│ Content-Type: application/json
│ → 200 / 201: success
│ → 4xx: business error — log, skip record, continue
│ → 429: rate limit — back off and retry
│ → 5xx: server error — retry up to 3 times with exponential back-off
│
├── 4. TRACK RESULT PER RECORD
│ { productId: "success" | "failed" | "skipped" }
│
├── 5. CONTINUE TO NEXT RECORD
│ Do not abort entire batch on a single record failure
│
└── 6. POST-RUN SUMMARY
If any records failed → raise alert via Anypoint monitoring
Store failed record IDs for manual replay or next-run retry

4-product-sync4. Product Sync
-----------------------------

### 41-trigger4.1 Trigger

AP21 product create or update event consumed by MuleSoft. Can be event-driven (real-time per product) or scheduled batch.

### 42-api-endpoints4.2 API Endpoints

| Operation | Method | Endpoint | When |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Create master | `POST` | `/product/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/products/{catalogId}` | Product does not exist |
| Update master | `PUT` | `/product/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/products/{catalogId}/{productId}` | Product exists |
| Create variant | `POST` | `/product/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/products/{catalogId}` | Variant does not exist — after master created |
| Update variant | `PUT` | `/product/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/products/{catalogId}/{productId}` | Variant exists |
| Assign to category | `PUT` | `/product/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/categories/{categoryId}/products/{productId}` | After product created |

For a batch of 1,000 products × 5 variants = 12,000 API calls (6,000 existence checks + 6,000 writes).

5-price-sync--filebased-only5. Price Sync — File-Based Only
-----------------------------------------------------------

> ⚠️ **No SCAPI Admin API exists for writing pricebook entries.**
>
> This has been confirmed against Salesforce developer documentation — no SCAPI Admin API for pricebook entry writes exists as a published endpoint. OCAPI is deprecated and must not be used for new integrations.
>
> **Price sync must use the file-based pricebook XML import regardless of which pattern is chosen for products and inventory.**

### 51-mechanism5.1 Mechanism

Pricebook XML delivered via WebDAV + `sfcc-site-archive-import` job — identical to the file-based design. See [TSD: Catalogue Sync — Product, Price & Inventory — Section 5](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/312508418) for the full specification.

### 52-scope5.2 Scope

Domestic sites only — AU, UK, US, EU. International sites (USIntl, EUIntl, HK, ME) pricing is managed by Global-e.

| Site | List Pricebook ID | Sale Pricebook ID |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ZimmermannAU | `au-aud-list-prices` | `au-aud-sale-prices` |
| ZimmermannUK | `uk-gbp-list-prices` | `uk-gbp-sale-prices` |
| ZimmermannUS | `us-usd-list-prices` | `us-usd-sale-prices` |
| ZimmermannEU | `eu-eur-list-prices` | `eu-eur-sale-prices` |

### 53-implication-for-hybrid-pattern5.3 Implication for Hybrid Pattern

If Zimmermann selects SCAPI Admin API for product and inventory sync, MuleSoft must still implement the WebDAV + job-trigger flow for price sync. Both flows co-exist:

* **Product + Inventory** → SCAPI Admin API per-record calls
* **Price** → WebDAV pricebook XML + `sfcc-site-archive-import` job

---

6-inventory-sync6. Inventory Sync
---------------------------------

### 61-trigger6.1 Trigger

Every 15 minutes per region (AU, GB, US). EU, EUIntl, HK, ME coverage to be confirmed — see open item #3.

### 62-source6.2 Source

NewStore S3 availability export → MuleSoft decompresses and transforms to SCAPI Inventory Lists API payloads.

### 63-api-reference6.3 API Reference

[SCAPI Inventory Lists API](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/commerce-api/references/inventory-lists) — Admin API, AmOAuth2 auth.

**Base path:**Defaultnonehttps://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com

| Operation | Method | Endpoint | Notes |

| Create or update inventory record | `PUT` | `/inventory/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/inventory-lists/{listId}/product-inventory-records/{productId}` | Full replace of record |
| Partial update inventory record | `PATCH` | `/inventory/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/inventory-lists/{listId}/product-inventory-records/{productId}` | Update specific fields only. Negative allocation amounts are disallowed |
| Get inventory record | `GET` | `/inventory/v1/organizations/{organizationId}/inventory-lists/{listId}/product-inventory-records/{productId}` | Read current record before update if needed |

Use `PUT` for a full inventory record write from NewStore (all fields known). Use `PATCH` only for targeted partial corrections (e.g. adjusting `allocation` only after a manual stock adjustment). For the standard 15-minute NewStore sync, `PUT` is the correct method.

Contentful is the sole CMS across all Zimmermann storefronts (HPC-001). It manages editorial content,

**Architecture:** Single Contentful space with one environment per delivery tier.
Environment IDs match SFCC tier names exactly — no mapping required at runtime.

Environment Topology
--------------------

Six-tier delivery pipeline. Contentful environment IDs map directly to MRT push targets.

| Tier | Name | Contentful Env ID | MRT Push Command | MRT URL |

| 1 & 2 | DEV | `dev` | `npm run push:dev` | zimmermann-dev.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |

| 6 | UAT | `uat` | `npm run push:uat` | zimmermann-uat.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |
| 7 | PRODUCTION | `master` (via `production` alias) | `npm run push:prod` | zimmermann-production.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |

Promotion order: **dev → test → sit → staging → uat → master**

Alias Strategy & Release Workflow
---------------------------------

Two aliases are maintained and always kept in sync:

* `production` — what MRT production tier uses (`CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID=production`). Flipping this is the zero-downtime release mechanism.
* `master` — Contentful’s built-in alias, kept in sync with `production`.

### Release workflow

1. Create a release environment in the Contentful web UI: clone from the current `production` target, name it `release-YYYY-MM`.
2. Run migrations: `npm run migrate:contentful -- --target release-YYYY-MM`
3. Test against the release environment directly (bypasses the alias).
4. Promote: `npm run promote:alias -- --target release-YYYY-MM` (flips both aliases atomically).
5. Retain the previous environment for 14 days as a rollback target, then delete.

The `production` alias requires the Contentful Enterprise plan. The `master` alias is always available as the built-in fallback.

API Keys & Tokens
-----------------

| Variable | Scope | Local .env | GitHub Actions | MRT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` | Space (shared) | ✓ | Variable | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` | Per tier | ✓ | Variable per env | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` | Per env, read-only | ✓ | Variable per env | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` | Per env, server-side only | ✓ | Secret per env | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Per user (personal) | ✓ | Secret (CI service account) | **Never** |
| `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Per env | ✓ | Secret per env | ✓ per tier |

### CI service account CMA token

Create a dedicated Contentful user (e.g. `contentful-ci@zimmermann.com`), invite as Space Administrator,
log in as that user and generate a Personal Access Token under Account Settings → CMA Tokens.
Store as the `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` GitHub Actions secret.

### Per-developer setup

Each developer generates their own CMA token: **Contentful → top-right avatar → Account Settings → CMA Tokens → Create personal access token**.
Add it to local `.env` as `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`. Delivery and preview tokens are space-level — run `npm run config:contentful` to populate them automatically.

Locale Configuration
--------------------

Nine locales matching SFCC `config/sites.js` exactly. No runtime mapping required.

| Locale Code | Name | Storefront(s) | Fallback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `en` | English (AU) | ZimmermannAU | Default |
| `en-US` | English (US) | ZimmermannUS | en |
| `en-GB` | English (UK / EU) | ZimmermannUK, ZimmermannEUen | en |

| `en-HK` | English (HK) | ZimmermannHK | en |
| `en-AE` | English (ME) | ZimmermannME | en |

Locales are created in the `master` environment during bootstrap; cloned environments inherit them automatically. All translatable fields use `localized: true`; structural fields (asset links, product IDs) use `localized: false`.

Content Type Management
-----------------------

|  | Editorial content types | Studio Experiences definitions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Location** | `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js` | `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/*ContentfulDefinition.ts` |
| **Deploy** | `npm run sync:contentful` or migration | Imported at runtime — no push step |
| **Current types** | shoppableImage | CollectionHero, ImageText, ShoppableImage |

* **Contentful roles:** Assign a “Content Editor” role on `sit`, `staging`, `uat`, and `master` that can CRUD entries/assets but cannot edit content types. Only the CI service account can modify content types in those environments.
* **Migration runner** calls `detectDrift` automatically before applying. Use `--force` to bypass.

## Confluence Audit — SFCC-122 & SFCC-123

Searched the full SFCC space (147 pages) rather than relying on my prior index — found a whole "05.3 — Integration" section with directly relevant TSDs that I hadn't previously surfaced.

### SFCC-122 — MRT API Capabilities

**No single canonical doc exists.** The spike is genuinely needed, not duplicative work. Closest useful material:

- **[TSD: Catalogue Sync — SCAPI Admin API Design (Alternative Pattern)](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/315490342)** — the best existing answer. Documents SCAPI Admin APIs for Product and Inventory as an alternative to the recommended WebDAV file-based import, with full endpoint/auth/error-handling detail. **Critical finding baked in: no SCAPI Admin API exists for writing pricebook/price data** — pricing must always go through file-based WebDAV import, regardless of which pattern is chosen for product/inventory. That's a hard architectural constraint directly relevant to your "which MRT APIs can serve product, category, and pricing data" task — the answer for pricing is "none, it's not achievable via API at all."

### SFCC-123 — Contentful Integration TSD

**Strong head start already exists** — much more coverage than SFCC-122.

- **[Contentful CMS — Setup & Operations](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/318472193)** — covers environment topology (7-tier, mapped 1:1 to MRT push targets), alias/release workflow, token scoping, and a locale table (9 locale codes across the 8 storefronts). - **[TSD: Product — SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/292061208) §6** — already states the handoff boundary you're asked to define: Contentful owns only editorial content (banners, collection pages, lookbook, rich PDP copy) via the Delivery API; all product/price/inventory data stays in SFCC via AP21→MuleSoft, never Contentful.

- **Dependencies tracker** row **T1 "Contentful CMS Readiness"** — same situation as T2: tracked, but SME Owner/Status/Notes blank.

### One discrepancy worth flagging

Both locale tables I found (Contentful ops page and the Product TSD) independently agree on **9** locale codes across the 8 storefronts. Worth resolving which figure is correct before it gets baked into a finalized Contentful locale setup — I haven't raised this with anyone yet.

- BOPIS (Collect in Boutique) checkout flow
- Full multi-site routing — 8 SFCC sites across 6 regions (AU, US domestic, US international, UK, EU domestic, EU international, HK, ME). **US site topology updated (REG-005, 2026-07-10):** US splits into two separate SFCC sites — US domestic (`/us/`, SFCC checkout) and US international (`/en-ca/`, Global-e checkout). New site ID `ZimmermannUSIntl` pending BM confirmation.
- Address autocomplete via Google Maps API
- Narvar EDD + tracking integration
- SEO: hreflang, canonical URLs, sitemaps
- Order-on-behalf (OOBO) for CS agents
- Retail Rewards (AP21) integration
- Gift card PDP, cart, checkout, and GiveX integration
- Promotions engine and multi-currency/FX pricebook setup
- CI workflow split — two complementary workflows, each with a clear role:
  - `qa.yml` (every PR to `develop`/`release/**`): `unit-tests` (Vitest) + `storybook-test` (Storybook `play` + `@storybook/addon-a11y`, `storybook test --ci`) run in parallel; `e2e-browserstack` on release PRs only. **`storybook-test` job is wired but pending `@storybook/addon-test` and `@storybook/addon-a11y` installation (feature/storybook-v10 upgrade task).**
  - `digital-sit.yml` (push/PR to `release/**`): four parallel jobs into `sit-gate` — `playwright-p0` (Chromium P0 suite), `bundle-size` (bundlewatch, main.js < 180 kB / vendor.js < 250 kB / main.css < 50 kB), `contract-tests` (placeholder; real MuleSoft OpenAPI assertion pending spec source), `lighthouse-ci` (Perf ≥ 80, A11y ≥ 90, Best Practices ≥ 90; requires LHCI server secrets)

## Unresolved Dependencies
Do not hard-code assumptions for the following — ask the user before implementing:
- Product copy ownership: Contentful vs SFCC vs AP21 (TBD).
- Translation trigger workflow with TransPerfect (TBD).
- Global-e + Didomi consent interaction (TBD).
- **Social login (Apple/Google):** Confirmed in scope for launch (ENH-004, Must-Have, Go-Live) as SFCC OOTB configuration only. **Hard dependency:** Apple and Google merchant accounts must be provisioned by Zimmermann before implementation can start. Do not implement until merchant accounts exist.
- **Omneo guest record creation timing:** When to create an Omneo record for a guest (at newsletter sign-up, at back-in-stock capture, at checkout, or only at order completion) is under legal/SFCC best-practice review. SFCC best practice is order completion only. Do not create Omneo records for guests at any earlier point until confirmed. Note: CRM-012–015 are signed off but Tony Tilbrook (early creation) and Izzy Coxon (order-completion only) currently disagree on the timing — treat as Open until reconciled.
- **Denmark routing:** Which storefront Denmark resolves to is not yet confirmed.
- **EU billing fields:** Locale-specific billing fields (Italian Codice Fiscale, Spanish NIF, French SIRET) — to be confirmed before implementing.
- **Adyen dynamic checkout (ENH-020):** Confirmed Must-Have for Go-Live, but a **hard dependency on Adyen** delivering A/B-able dynamic payment-method display. Do not assume the feature is buildable end-to-end until Adyen delivery is confirmed.
- **Optimizely SFCC data-layer scope (AAB-004):** Load mechanism Confirmed (PWA-direct head tag, US-only, Zimmermann-provided script). Residual: Tell No Lies suspects no SFCC-side data-layer work is needed for Optimizely (Magento launch was GTM-only). Confirm with Tell No Lies before doing SFCC data-layer work specifically for Optimizely.
- **CRM-155 customer group precedence:** Rules for resolving overlapping customer group memberships are TBD.
- **Mulesoft stock aggregation (CAI-023):** Confirmation pending that Mulesoft can aggregate warehouse + boutique stock pre-checkout.
- **Search/recommendation platform:** SFCC Einstein is confirmed on the Search sheet (SPR-63). **Cross-sheet contradiction (flag, do not resolve):** the Cart & Inventory sheet CAI-005 now states "search / recommendation engine not confirmed" with RJ noting "99% likely we will move away from Athos" — i.e. the engine is being treated as open there. Confirm which sheet is authoritative before relying on Einstein for cart/recommendation surfaces.
- **PRC-45 Retail Rewards count per order:** Requirement text says "maximum of one Retail Reward per order" but RJ challenges: "Multiple retail rewards can be applied per order." Downgraded to Open — confirm the cap before building reward-application logic.
- **Addingwell role in analytics (AAB-001/003):** AAB-001 frames all container/tag logic as living in GTM (Tell No Lies), while the Third Party Integrations rows say the GTM container loads *via the Addingwell MRT integration* and GA4/downstream tags route through an Addingwell *server-side container*. Reconciled in analytics.md as logic-vs-transport, but confirm with Tell No Lies whether Addingwell is none / transport-only / server-side routing.
- **DMU-007 order history source (upstream):** DMU-007 PWA contract Confirmed (displays MuleSoft payload). Residual upstream conflict: requirement + JT say NewStore via MuleSoft; RJ says "Order history will come from Omneo." Out of PWA boundary — reconcile so the integration contract is unambiguous.
- **DMU-009 Contentful setup ownership:** RJ: "This is no longer required as AS will be setting up Contentful." Downgraded pending reconciliation of who owns CMS setup.
- **Customer migration shape (DMU-004):** Only email + Omneo ID migrated; name, phone, addresses, comms prefs sourced **live from Omneo at login**. My Account profile pages must round-trip to Omneo post-auth. Graceful degradation for Omneo outages on account screens is now load-bearing — confirm UX before implementing profile reads.
- **Asset/CDN migration & platform (DMU-010 / DMU-020):** Asset migration de-scoped — no asset 301s; images stay in Contentful. Separately, the source note now records the platform CDN as Akamai (SFCC default), which sits against existing Cloudflare carry-forward references — confirm the CDN platform of record (no asset-migration impact either way).
- **PRC-43 Global-e cartridge customer-group catalogue prices:** Open with Global-e — does the cartridge honour customer-group catalogue prices (VIC) at international checkout? Also: how do VIC customers currently receive discounts at Global-e checkout in M2? Do not assume VIC pricing flows through Global-e until confirmed.
- **CFD-070 guest account creation flow:** Dependent on the guest journey design — open.
- **CFD-045 BOPIS seeding mechanism:** Open — how Collect in Boutique availability is seeded into checkout still TBC.
- **PAY-022 Adyen CVC config:** Confirm CVC-on-saved-card configuration with Adyen. PWA behaviour (re-entry required) is Confirmed.
- **PAY-047/048/049 fraud hold scope:** Adyen/NewStore-owned per IC; PWA-side display behaviour not yet signed off.
- **OM-002 MuleSoft order export gating:** Sign-off pending on the exact attribute set passed at order export.
- **OM-017/018 NewStore order status taxonomy:** SFCC displays raw MuleSoft status; mapping list still open.
- **OM-034 back-in-stock FIFO email logic:** Sign-off pending.
- **DLV-012 free-shipping thresholds:** Per-delivery-method per-storefront rate card updated; re-sign-off pending.
- **CAI-041 location-aware boutique inventory fallback:** Flagged as potential enhancement (RJ 25.05) — not in launch scope until confirmed.
- **RRC-030 tax/duties display location:** Confirm whether tax/duties appear in My Account vs Narvar/Global-e portals only.
- **CRM-022 international Retail Rewards via Global-e:** Not scoped; needs Global-e discussion.
- **CRM-048 / CRM-100 saved-address cap:** RJ proposes 20; IC "we can do this" — working target 20, formal sign-off pending.
- **DMU-018 / DMU-019 / DMU-022 SEO migration items:** Sparro dependencies — confirm before any URL-rewrite / canonical work. (DMU-016 closed 2026-06-04: REG-009 bot allowlist keeps AU root globally crawlable, so `x-default` stays AU.)
- **DMU-032 / DMU-035 SEO meta-title and schema authoring:** DMU-031 dropped the word "Online" from product meta-title format (`[Product Name] [Colour] | Zimmermann`); DMU-032 "auto-applied" question remains; DMU-035 schema definition still open with Sparro.
- **Wishlist hosting — SFCC vs Omneo (ENH-038/039):** Previously out of scope (wishlist to migrate to Omneo); now "ACN to size — wishlist in SFCC" / "To be sized." A SFCC-hosted wishlist for go-live is being scoped but NOT confirmed. ENH-040 still logs an eventual SFCC→Omneo migration. Note: Move-to-Wishlist (CAI-004/008) is **confirmed authenticated-only** at launch — guests are prompted to log in; guest wishlist is a logged enhancement out of scope for go-live.
- **Returns-link eligibility logic (ENH-014):** To be sized. Intended logic (not yet confirmed): show the Returns link only if the order contains returnable items (via product attribute); window = 15 days from delivery completion date, else 28 days from order creation date if no delivery completion date. Hard dependency: the delivery completion date must be passed back via MuleSoft.
- **Address validation on free-text addresses (CFD-024):** PO Box / Parcel Locker blocking is Confirmed. NEW VR/RT review request (not scoped): "Current magento behaviour lets a user checkout with a very random address with no error messaging. Can this be reviewed?" — broader address-validity enhancement, unscoped.
- **SSO scope (CRM-001):** Sheet only says "to be considered for go-live (ENH tab — to be discussed)". Treat as Open. Note: Social login (Apple/Google) is separately confirmed via ENH-004 (see entry above) and is the only SSO surface in scope for launch.
- **PRC-46 coupon handling at Global-e:** Workbook shows Confirmed 2026-06-24, but sign-off is conditional — "only if Global-e can support." Confirm with Global-e that the SFCC cartridge can apply and validate coupon codes at international checkout before implementing.
- **PRC-53 Global-e digital gift card currencies:** Currency coverage for digital gift cards at Global-e checkout to be confirmed.

content.content:
1	# 01 — Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SCAPI) + reCAPTCHA
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Salesforce Commerce Cloud B2C (SFCC) is the system of record for commerce data. The storefront calls SFCC directly from the browser via SCAPI for browsing, basket management, customer accounts, and order placement.
6	
7	In scope:
8	
9	- Authentication via Shopper Login & API Access Service (SLAS)
10	- Product catalogue, categories, search, recommendations
11	- Basket and cart
12	- Customer account (authentication record) and saved-payment token references
13	- Order placement for SFCC-owned checkouts (domestic markets)
14	- Gift cards — the storefront applies them via SCAPI; server-side redemption is outside the PWA boundary
15	- Google reCAPTCHA — browser-side script load on register/login forms; MRT-side token verification before SCAPI submission
16	
17	At migration, only the customer's email and Omneo ID are stored in SFCC. Name, phone, addresses, and communication preferences come from Omneo at login (DMU-004). Order history comes from MuleSoft via the MRT proxy, not from SFCC (DMU-007).
18	
19	Out of scope of this document:
20	
21	- GiveX validate/redeem/refund, Avalara tax, Adyen back-office — all server-side, outside the PWA
22	- SFCC ↔ MuleSoft flows to NewStore, AP21, Omneo, Narvar
23	- Booxi appointment booking — MRT-mediated (PWA → MRT → Booxi), not a SFCC flow
24	- Business Manager configuration: promotions rules, content slots, Page Designer pages
25	
26	## 2. Browser-side architecture
27	
28	```
29	PWA (React, SSR + CSR)
30	        │
31	        │  @salesforce/commerce-sdk-react (TanStack Query under the hood)
32	        ▼
33	SLAS auth (guest or registered shopper) ──► Shopper context
34	        │                                       (site, currency, locale, customer)
35	        ▼
36	SCAPI: products, search, baskets, orders, customers, promotions, gift cards
37	        │
38	        ▼
39	SFCC realm
40	```
41	
42	- **Single SDK.** `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` handles every SFCC call — SLAS token lifecycle, retry, and TanStack Query caching.
43	- **SSR and CSR.** Catalogue, PDP, PLP, content, and boutique pages are server-rendered for SEO and LCP. Cart, checkout, My Account, and order pages render an SSR shell and hydrate personalised data client-side after auth.
44	- **Managed Runtime.** The PWA Kit Node layer hosts the SSR pipeline and routes SLAS private-client calls through the server-side proxy.
45	
46	## 3. Authentication and credentials
47	
48	- **SLAS private-client flow** issues two token types: a guest access token (anonymous shopper, refreshed silently) and a registered shopper access token (issued after email/password login). Tokens are JWTs with a customer ID, unique shopper ID (USID), and refresh token.
49	- **Refresh tokens live in `httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` cookies** set by the SSR layer. Browser JavaScript never sees the raw refresh token. On each refresh SLAS regenerates the token and voids the old one; the SSR layer rewrites the cookie in the same response.
50	- **Private client credentials.** The SLAS client secret is an MRT environment variable and never reaches the browser. The authorisation code exchange goes through the MRT private-client proxy (`privateClientProxyEndpoint`). The SLAS client ID and SCAPI short code stay in the bundle as public identifiers.
51	- **Social login.** Apple and Google via SLAS third-party identity-provider federation — confirmed in scope for launch; implementation design still open.
52	- **No Open Commerce API (OCAPI) credentials in the browser.** Any operation not yet covered by SCAPI is proxied through Managed Runtime with OCAPI credentials held server-side.
53	
54	### Magento password migration (CFD-013)
55	
56	Passwords were not migrated from Magento. All existing customers must reset at go-live. Failed sign-ins return a generic "invalid credentials" message (no email-existence leak) and the "forgot password" link is always visible.
57	
58	### Cross-storefront session continuity
59	
60	All eight storefronts are path-prefixed on a single domain and share one SFCC realm.
61	
62	- **The refresh-token cookie is shared across storefronts.** Every storefront lives on the same domain, so the `httpOnly` cookie is sent on every path prefix. No cross-domain SSO bridge is needed.
63	- **Tokens are channel-scoped.** A token issued for `zimm-au` is not valid for `zimm-uk` — this is a hard SLAS platform constraint. On a storefront switch the SSR layer performs a fresh authorisation for the destination channel using the SLAS Trusted System on Behalf (TSOB) flow: it calls `getTrustedSystemAccessToken` with the shopper's `login_id`, which issues a new channel-scoped token server-side without prompting the customer. A registered shopper stays signed in transparently. A guest session does not carry over — guest tokens and baskets are site-scoped. **TSOB rate limit:** SLAS returns HTTP 409 if multiple TSOB calls are made for the same shopper within a 3-second window — the SSR layer must not fire duplicate TSOB calls on rapid storefront switches (debounce or dedupe at the MRT layer).
64	- **Baskets do not transfer — by design.** Baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency. Switching storefront starts a fresh basket; carrying one across a currency boundary would produce wrong prices.
65	- **Checkout handoff is a separate boundary.** When handing off to Global-e, the SLAS session does not extend into Global-e's hosted checkout.
66	
67	## 4. Data exchanged
68	
69	| Resource                           | Verbs                    | Notes                                                                                                                                           |
70	| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
71	| `/checkout/shopper-login/oauth2/*` | GET, POST                | SLAS authentication and token lifecycle                                                                                                         |
72	| `/product/shopper-products/v1/*`   | GET                      | Product details, master/variant resolution                                                                                                      |
73	| `/search/shopper-search/v1/*`      | GET                      | Catalogue search, faceting, sort, suggestions                                                                                                   |
74	| `/checkout/shopper-baskets/v2/*`   | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE | Basket lifecycle, line items, shipments, payment instruments                                                                                    |
75	| `/checkout/shopper-orders/v1/*`    | POST, GET                | Order placement and lookup (SFCC-owned checkouts only)                                                                                          |
76	| `/customer/shopper-customers/v1/*` | GET, POST, PATCH         | Profile, addresses, saved-payment references                                                                                                    |
77	| `/pricing/shopper-promotions/v1/*` | GET                      | Active promotions, coupon validation                                                                                                            |
78	| Einstein recommendations endpoints | GET                      | Personalised recommendations slot. Consent-gated (Didomi purpose TBC) — falls back to a static SFCC merchandising group if consent is not given |
79	
80	Every request carries the site ID, organisation ID, locale, currency, and SLAS bearer token. PII travels over TLS only. PCI scope is Adyen's — SFCC holds token references only.
81	
82	## 5. reCAPTCHA on register and login (CRM-008)
83	
84	- The storefront loads the reCAPTCHA v3 script on register and login forms only — not on any other page — and only after the customer first touches the form, so the script never blocks first paint.
85	- On submit, the reCAPTCHA token is sent alongside the form data to the MRT layer. The MRT layer verifies the token against Google's `siteverify` endpoint (using the secret key held as the `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` MRT environment variable) before forwarding the request to SCAPI. The secret key never reaches the browser.
86	- The site key is set per environment as `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` (MRT environment variable, public). The secret key is held as `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` (MRT environment variable, server-only).
87	- reCAPTCHA loads on form interaction regardless of consent. **Exception: EU and UK** — in those regions it only loads after Didomi consent, which means a visitor who declines gets no bot protection there.
88	
89	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
90	
91	- **HTTP/2** to a single SCAPI host; `<link rel="preconnect">` emitted in the document head.
92	- **TanStack Query** dedupes in-flight requests. Working defaults: stale time 60 s for catalogue, 30 s for promotions, 0 s for basket (always fresh).
93	- **SFCC edge cache** for anonymous catalogue traffic; cache keys include site, locale, currency, and customer group.
94	- **Parallel calls on PDP.** Product, recommendations, and promotions are fetched in parallel — no waterfall.
95	- **SSR fetches only critical data.** Recommendations and reviews load client-side after hydration.
96	- **Field projection.** SCAPI `fields=` parameters are used where supported to reduce payload size.
97	
98	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
99	
100	SFCC site IDs and Business Manager locale IDs verified against bkzk-002 Business Manager (2026-06-13):
101	
102	| SFCC Site ID               | BM Locale ID                                  | URL prefix                                 | Currency               | Checkout owner              |
103	| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------- | --------------------------- |
104	| `ZimmermannAU`             | `en`                                          | `/` (root, x-default hreflang)             | AUD                    | SFCC                        |
105	| `ZimmermannUS`             | `en-US`                                       | `/us/`                                     | USD                    | SFCC (US domestic)          |
106	| `ZimmermannUSIntl` _(TBC)_ | `en-US` _(TBC)_                               | `/en-ca/`                                  | USD                    | Global-e (US international) |
107	| `ZimmermannUK`             | `en-GB`                                       | `/uk/`                                     | GBP                    | SFCC                        |
108	| `ZimmermannEU`             | `en-GB` (EN), `fr` (FR), `it` (IT), `es` (ES) | `/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/` | EUR                    | SFCC                        |
109	| `ZimmermannEUIntl`         | `en-CH`                                       | `/en-ch/`                                  | EUR                    | Global-e                    |
110	| `ZimmermannHK`             | `en-HK`                                       | `/hk/`                                     | HKD (SFCC price books) | Global-e                    |
111	| `ZimmermannME`             | `en-AE`                                       | `/en-ae/`                                  | AED (SFCC price books) | Global-e                    |
112	
113	- The site ID is resolved from the URL prefix on every request (SSR and CSR).
114	- AU is geo-redirected for non-Oceania human visitors; verified search bots and social unfurlers are exempt via UA allowlist.

128	| reCAPTCHA fails to load or token rejected     | Block the register/login submit, show a "please retry" message, and offer a contact-support path after two failures.                                                            |

133	- SLAS private-client flow — the authorisation code exchange is proxied through MRT so the client secret never reaches the browser.

# 01 — Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SCAPI) + reCAPTCHA

## 1. Purpose and scope

Salesforce Commerce Cloud B2C (SFCC) is the system of record for commerce data. The storefront calls SFCC directly from the browser via SCAPI for browsing, basket management, customer accounts, and order placement.

In scope:

- Authentication via Shopper Login & API Access Service (SLAS)
- Product catalogue, categories, search, recommendations
- Basket and cart
- Customer account (authentication record) and saved-payment token references
- Order placement for SFCC-owned checkouts (domestic markets)
- Gift cards — the storefront applies them via SCAPI; server-side redemption is outside the PWA boundary
- Google reCAPTCHA — browser-side script load on register/login forms; MRT-side token verification before SCAPI submission

At migration, only the customer's email and Omneo ID are stored in SFCC. Name, phone, addresses, and communication preferences come from Omneo at login (DMU-004). Order history comes from MuleSoft via the MRT proxy, not from SFCC (DMU-007).

Out of scope of this document:

- GiveX validate/redeem/refund, Avalara tax, Adyen back-office — all server-side, outside the PWA
- SFCC ↔ MuleSoft flows to NewStore, AP21, Omneo, Narvar
- Booxi appointment booking — MRT-mediated (PWA → MRT → Booxi), not a SFCC flow
- Business Manager configuration: promotions rules, content slots, Page Designer pages

## 2. Browser-side architecture

```
PWA (React, SSR + CSR)
        │
        │  @salesforce/commerce-sdk-react (TanStack Query under the hood)
        ▼
SLAS auth (guest or registered shopper) ──► Shopper context
        │                                       (site, currency, locale, customer)
        ▼
SCAPI: products, search, baskets, orders, customers, promotions, gift cards
        │
        ▼
SFCC realm
```

- **Single SDK.** `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` handles every SFCC call — SLAS token lifecycle, retry, and TanStack Query caching.
- **SSR and CSR.** Catalogue, PDP, PLP, content, and boutique pages are server-rendered for SEO and LCP. Cart, checkout, My Account, and order pages render an SSR shell and hydrate personalised data client-side after auth.
- **Managed Runtime.** The PWA Kit Node layer hosts the SSR pipeline and routes SLAS private-client calls through the server-side proxy.

## 3. Authentication and credentials

- **SLAS private-client flow** issues two token types: a guest access token (anonymous shopper, refreshed silently) and a registered shopper access token (issued after email/password login). Tokens are JWTs with a customer ID, unique shopper ID (USID), and refresh token.
- **Refresh tokens live in `httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` cookies** set by the SSR layer. Browser JavaScript never sees the raw refresh token. On each refresh SLAS regenerates the token and voids the old one; the SSR layer rewrites the cookie in the same response.
- **Private client credentials.** The SLAS client secret is an MRT environment variable and never reaches the browser. The authorisation code exchange goes through the MRT private-client proxy (`privateClientProxyEndpoint`). The SLAS client ID and SCAPI short code stay in the bundle as public identifiers.
- **Social login.** Apple and Google via SLAS third-party identity-provider federation — confirmed in scope for launch; implementation design still open.
- **No Open Commerce API (OCAPI) credentials in the browser.** Any operation not yet covered by SCAPI is proxied through Managed Runtime with OCAPI credentials held server-side.

### Magento password migration (CFD-013)

Passwords were not migrated from Magento. All existing customers must reset at go-live. Failed sign-ins return a generic "invalid credentials" message (no email-existence leak) and the "forgot password" link is always visible.

### Cross-storefront session continuity

All eight storefronts are path-prefixed on a single domain and share one SFCC realm.

- **The refresh-token cookie is shared across storefronts.** Every storefront lives on the same domain, so the `httpOnly` cookie is sent on every path prefix. No cross-domain SSO bridge is needed.
- **Tokens are channel-scoped.** A token issued for `zimm-au` is not valid for `zimm-uk` — this is a hard SLAS platform constraint. On a storefront switch the SSR layer performs a fresh authorisation for the destination channel using the SLAS Trusted System on Behalf (TSOB) flow: it calls `getTrustedSystemAccessToken` with the shopper's `login_id`, which issues a new channel-scoped token server-side without prompting the customer. A registered shopper stays signed in transparently. A guest session does not carry over — guest tokens and baskets are site-scoped. **TSOB rate limit:** SLAS returns HTTP 409 if multiple TSOB calls are made for the same shopper within a 3-second window — the SSR layer must not fire duplicate TSOB calls on rapid storefront switches (debounce or dedupe at the MRT layer).
- **Baskets do not transfer — by design.** Baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency. Switching storefront starts a fresh basket; carrying one across a currency boundary would produce wrong prices.
- **Checkout handoff is a separate boundary.** When handing off to Global-e, the SLAS session does not extend into Global-e's hosted checkout.

## 4. Data exchanged

| Resource                           | Verbs                    | Notes                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/checkout/shopper-login/oauth2/*` | GET, POST                | SLAS authentication and token lifecycle                                                                                                         |
| `/product/shopper-products/v1/*`   | GET                      | Product details, master/variant resolution                                                                                                      |
| `/search/shopper-search/v1/*`      | GET                      | Catalogue search, faceting, sort, suggestions                                                                                                   |
| `/checkout/shopper-baskets/v2/*`   | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE | Basket lifecycle, line items, shipments, payment instruments                                                                                    |
| `/checkout/shopper-orders/v1/*`    | POST, GET                | Order placement and lookup (SFCC-owned checkouts only)                                                                                          |
| `/customer/shopper-customers/v1/*` | GET, POST, PATCH         | Profile, addresses, saved-payment references                                                                                                    |
| `/pricing/shopper-promotions/v1/*` | GET                      | Active promotions, coupon validation                                                                                                            |
| Einstein recommendations endpoints | GET                      | Personalised recommendations slot. Consent-gated (Didomi purpose TBC) — falls back to a static SFCC merchandising group if consent is not given |

Every request carries the site ID, organisation ID, locale, currency, and SLAS bearer token. PII travels over TLS only. PCI scope is Adyen's — SFCC holds token references only.

## 5. reCAPTCHA on register and login (CRM-008)

- The storefront loads the reCAPTCHA v3 script on register and login forms only — not on any other page — and only after the customer first touches the form, so the script never blocks first paint.
- On submit, the reCAPTCHA token is sent alongside the form data to the MRT layer. The MRT layer verifies the token against Google's `siteverify` endpoint (using the secret key held as the `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` MRT environment variable) before forwarding the request to SCAPI. The secret key never reaches the browser.
- The site key is set per environment as `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` (MRT environment variable, public). The secret key is held as `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` (MRT environment variable, server-only).
- reCAPTCHA loads on form interaction regardless of consent. **Exception: EU and UK** — in those regions it only loads after Didomi consent, which means a visitor who declines gets no bot protection there.

## 6. Performance and loading strategy

- **HTTP/2** to a single SCAPI host; `<link rel="preconnect">` emitted in the document head.
- **TanStack Query** dedupes in-flight requests. Working defaults: stale time 60 s for catalogue, 30 s for promotions, 0 s for basket (always fresh).
- **SFCC edge cache** for anonymous catalogue traffic; cache keys include site, locale, currency, and customer group.
- **Parallel calls on PDP.** Product, recommendations, and promotions are fetched in parallel — no waterfall.
- **SSR fetches only critical data.** Recommendations and reviews load client-side after hydration.
- **Field projection.** SCAPI `fields=` parameters are used where supported to reduce payload size.

## 7. Multi-region behaviour

SFCC site IDs and Business Manager locale IDs verified against bkzk-002 Business Manager (2026-06-13):

| SFCC Site ID               | BM Locale ID                                  | URL prefix                                 | Currency               | Checkout owner              |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `ZimmermannAU`             | `en`                                          | `/` (root, x-default hreflang)             | AUD                    | SFCC                        |
| `ZimmermannUS`             | `en-US`                                       | `/us/`                                     | USD                    | SFCC (US domestic)          |
| `ZimmermannUSIntl` _(TBC)_ | `en-US` _(TBC)_                               | `/en-ca/`                                  | USD                    | Global-e (US international) |
| `ZimmermannUK`             | `en-GB`                                       | `/uk/`                                     | GBP                    | SFCC                        |
| `ZimmermannEU`             | `en-GB` (EN), `fr` (FR), `it` (IT), `es` (ES) | `/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/` | EUR                    | SFCC                        |
| `ZimmermannEUIntl`         | `en-CH`                                       | `/en-ch/`                                  | EUR                    | Global-e                    |
| `ZimmermannHK`             | `en-HK`                                       | `/hk/`                                     | HKD (SFCC price books) | Global-e                    |
| `ZimmermannME`             | `en-AE`                                       | `/en-ae/`                                  | AED (SFCC price books) | Global-e                    |

- The site ID is resolved from the URL prefix on every request (SSR and CSR).
- AU is geo-redirected for non-Oceania human visitors; verified search bots and social unfurlers are exempt via UA allowlist.
- Per-environment SLAS client ID and SCAPI short code remain outstanding — see §11 item 2.

## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure                                       | Behaviour                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| SLAS unavailable                              | Storefront cannot mint a guest token and is non-operational. Show a maintenance message. P1 incident.                                                                           |
| SCAPI catalogue 5xx                           | TanStack Query retries three times with exponential backoff. On final failure, show the last cached payload if available; otherwise show an error state with a "Try again" CTA. |
| SCAPI basket 5xx during add-to-cart           | Inline error toast. The user's intent stays in client state so a retry resends the same request.                                                                                |
| Order placement 5xx after Adyen authorisation | Hard error — the order cannot fail silently. The customer sees an explicit error with a contact reference and ops is alerted.                                                   |
| Einstein recommendations 5xx                  | Hide the slot or fall back to a static merchandising group.                                                                                                                     |
| SLAS token refresh fails                      | Force re-login. The basket is preserved on the guest token until the customer completes checkout.                                                                               |
| TSOB 409 (rapid storefront switch)            | Retry after 3 seconds. Do not re-login the customer — the existing session is still valid on the origin channel.                                                                |
| reCAPTCHA fails to load or token rejected     | Block the register/login submit, show a "please retry" message, and offer a contact-support path after two failures.                                                            |

## 9. Security and privacy

- All traffic is TLS 1.2+ over HTTPS.
- SLAS private-client flow — the authorisation code exchange is proxied through MRT so the client secret never reaches the browser.
- Refresh tokens are held in `httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` cookies — never in browser JavaScript.
- PCI scope is Adyen's — the browser sends payment data directly to Adyen. SFCC holds token references only.

## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation

1. **Login MFA scope.** Confirm whether multi-factor authentication on login is in scope for launch or post-launch. If in scope, the SLAS configuration and the PWA login flow need additional design.

2. **`sfPayments.metadataUrl` hostname.** The `sfcc-payments` undici connection pool (TSD §12.1) holds `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl`'s origin in a pool separate from `sfcc-scapi` (`{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`). That separation only provides blast-radius isolation if the two hosts are different origins. If `sfPayments.metadataUrl` resolves to the same SCAPI host, the pools should be merged.

1	# 02 — Contentful (CMS)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Contentful is the headless CMS for editorial content: homepage modules, promotional banners, lookbooks, campaign landing pages, size guide fallback content (primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay — PRD-053), footer, and editorial blocks on PLPs and PDPs. The storefront reads published content via the **Delivery API (CDA)** from both SSR and the browser, reads draft content via the **Preview API (CPA)** in editor sessions, and receives **publish webhooks** to clear the SSR cache.
6	
7	In scope:
8	
9	- Reading published content via the Delivery API
10	- Reading draft content via the Preview API in editor preview sessions
11	- Live preview in Contentful Studio
12	- Locale-specific content via Contentful's native localisation
13	- Contentful Studio Experiences — drag-and-drop page composition by editors
14	- Receiving publish webhooks to clear stale SSR cache entries
15	
16	Out of scope of this document:
17	
18	- Content type schema sync (managed in code via the Management API — see §2)
19	- Asset uploads and content editing in Contentful Studio
20	- Webhooks from Contentful to SFCC (none planned)
21	
22	**Content ownership.** SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001). Rows marked *pending* are unconfirmed (see §11).
23	
24	| Surface | SFCC owns | Contentful owns | Status |
25	|---|---|---|---|
26	| Homepage | Commerce data for embedded product refs | All modules — hero, banners, campaign blocks | Confirmed |
27	| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
28	| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
29	| Size guides | — | Fallback content only — primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay (PRD-053, confirmed 2026-06-19); Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product | Updated |
30	| Footer | — | All content | Confirmed |
31	| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | *Whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful is pending* |
32	| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary size guide is Measmerize — PRD-053) | *Which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer is pending* |
33	| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | *Pending* |
34	| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy — managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005); clickable badges link to category/PLP. Contentful is not the source of badge content unless explicitly confirmed. | — | Confirmed |
35	
36	## 2. Content type management (build-time)
37	
38	Content type schemas are managed in code, not in the Contentful UI:
39	
40	- Schema definitions live in the PWA repo and are reviewed via pull request.
41	- A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
42	- Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time.
43	
44	## 3. Browser-side architecture
45	
46	```
47	PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
48	        │
49	        ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
50	        │        SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
51	        │        post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
52	        │
53	        ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
54	        │        Editor preview only. Token held server-side in MRT;
55	        │        never reaches the browser. Requests proxied through
56	        │        an MRT preview endpoint.
57	        │
58	        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
59	        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
60	        │
61	        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
62	                 Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
63	                 HMAC-verified with a shared secret.
64	```
65	
66	- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
67	- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
68	- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the storefront renders inside Studio's iframe. It detects the preview origin, switches to the CPA-backed MRT proxy, and refreshes on `postMessage` events from Studio.
69	- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.
70	
71	## 4. Authentication and credentials
72	
73	| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
74	|---|---|---|
75	| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
76	| Preview API token (CPA) | MRT preview proxy only | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. MRT environment variable. Never reaches the browser. |
77	| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
78	| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |
79	
80	Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.
81	
82	## 5. Data exchanged
83	
84	| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
85	|---|---|---|
86	| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
87	| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
88	| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
89	| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
90	| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |
91	
92	No PII flows through Contentful.
93	
94	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
95	
96	- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
97	- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
98	- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
99	- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
100	- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
101	- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.
102	
103	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
104	
105	- A single Contentful Space serves all eight storefronts via Contentful's native locale model.
106	- The active locale is resolved from the URL prefix and passed as `locale=` on every CDA request. Eleven active locales: en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE.
107	- Region-specific entries (banners, promotions, editorial that varies by site) are filtered at query time using the active SFCC site ID.
108	
109	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
110	
111	| Failure | Behaviour |
112	|---|---|
113	| Contentful CDA unavailable | Page renders without editorial content. Editorial slots show empty; commerce data is never blocked on a CMS read. |
114	| Stale cached content after a publish | Tolerated within the 60-second TTL. The publish webhook normally clears affected entries in seconds; the TTL is the safety net if the webhook drops. |
115	| Preview API returns broken or unpublished refs | Editor preview only — render a placeholder. Production traffic never hits this path. |
116	| Asset (image) 404 | Show alt text and a graceful placeholder. |
117	| 429 rate limit on CDA | Exponential backoff and retry. The SSR cache makes this rare in practice. |
118	| Publish webhook fails HMAC verification | Reject and log. Storefront continues serving from cache; the TTL picks up the change. |
119	| Live preview iframe disconnects | Storefront silently returns to non-preview mode. |
120	
121	## 9. Security and privacy
122	
123	- The CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment. Embedding in the bundle is safe per Contentful's published guidance.
124	- The CPA token is held server-side only and is never logged.
125	- The CMA token is held only on the CI host — never embedded, never in PR diffs.
126	- No PII is handled by Contentful.
127	
128	## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation
129	
130	1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all eight storefronts.
131	2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC owns all commerce data, Contentful owns editorial. Not yet confirmed is the split on composed pages: which editorial blocks appear on PDP and PLP, whether they are authored in SFCC Page Designer or Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or built in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu includes Contentful-authored promotional tiles. The working assumption is in the ownership table in §1.
132	3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provide per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be tested against a real Contentful environment.
133

- Webhooks from Contentful to SFCC (none planned)

**Content ownership.** SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001). Rows marked *pending* are unconfirmed (see §11).

| Surface | SFCC owns | Contentful owns | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Homepage | Commerce data for embedded product refs | All modules — hero, banners, campaign blocks | Confirmed |
| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
| Size guides | — | Fallback content only — primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay (PRD-053, confirmed 2026-06-19); Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product | Updated |
| Footer | — | All content | Confirmed |
| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | *Whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful is pending* |
| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary size guide is Measmerize — PRD-053) | *Which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer is pending* |
| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | *Pending* |
| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy — managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005); clickable badges link to category/PLP. Contentful is not the source of badge content unless explicitly confirmed. | — | Confirmed |

## 2. Content type management (build-time)

Content type schemas are managed in code, not in the Contentful UI:

- Schema definitions live in the PWA repo and are reviewed via pull request.
- A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
- Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time.

## 3. Browser-side architecture

```
PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
        │
        ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
        │        SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
        │        post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
        │
        ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
        │        Editor preview only. Token held server-side in MRT;
        │        never reaches the browser. Requests proxied through
        │        an MRT preview endpoint.
        │
        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
        │
        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
                 Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
                 HMAC-verified with a shared secret.
```

- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the storefront renders inside Studio's iframe. It detects the preview origin, switches to the CPA-backed MRT proxy, and refreshes on `postMessage` events from Studio.
- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.

## 4. Authentication and credentials

| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
|---|---|---|
| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
| Preview API token (CPA) | MRT preview proxy only | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. MRT environment variable. Never reaches the browser. |
| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |

Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.

## 5. Data exchanged

| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |

No PII flows through Contentful.

## 6. Performance and loading strategy

- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.

## 7. Multi-region behaviour

- A single Contentful Space serves all eight storefronts via Contentful's native locale model.
- The active locale is resolved from the URL prefix and passed as `locale=` on every CDA request. Eleven active locales: en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE.
- Region-specific entries (banners, promotions, editorial that varies by site) are filtered at query time using the active SFCC site ID.

## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Contentful CDA unavailable | Page renders without editorial content. Editorial slots show empty; commerce data is never blocked on a CMS read. |
| Stale cached content after a publish | Tolerated within the 60-second TTL. The publish webhook normally clears affected entries in seconds; the TTL is the safety net if the webhook drops. |
| Preview API returns broken or unpublished refs | Editor preview only — render a placeholder. Production traffic never hits this path. |
| Asset (image) 404 | Show alt text and a graceful placeholder. |
| 429 rate limit on CDA | Exponential backoff and retry. The SSR cache makes this rare in practice. |
| Publish webhook fails HMAC verification | Reject and log. Storefront continues serving from cache; the TTL picks up the change. |
| Live preview iframe disconnects | Storefront silently returns to non-preview mode. |

## 9. Security and privacy

- The CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment. Embedding in the bundle is safe per Contentful's published guidance.
- The CPA token is held server-side only and is never logged.
- The CMA token is held only on the CI host — never embedded, never in PR diffs.
- No PII is handled by Contentful.

## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation

1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all eight storefronts.
2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC owns all commerce data, Contentful owns editorial. Not yet confirmed is the split on composed pages: which editorial blocks appear on PDP and PLP, whether they are authored in SFCC Page Designer or Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or built in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu includes Contentful-authored promotional tiles. The working assumption is in the ownership table in §1.
3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provide per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be tested against a real Contentful environment.
