1	# 03 — MuleSoft (PWA-direct reads via MRT proxy)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	MuleSoft is the integration middleware that sits between SFCC and Zimmermann's back-office systems (NewStore OMS, AP21, Omneo, Narvar). The vast majority of MuleSoft traffic is server-to-server from SFCC and is out of scope here. This document covers the **separate, direct path** in which the PWA's Managed Runtime Node layer calls MuleSoft directly via `/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...` for a small set of read operations where SFCC adds no value to the round-trip.
6	
7	Operations in scope of this document (PWA → MRT → MuleSoft, with SFCC outside the read path):
8	
9	- Order history list (CRM-056 / CRM-057, RRC-013) — the 50 most recent orders, online and in-store
10	- Order detail (CRM-071 / CRM-072)
11	- Account dashboard "recent orders" summary (CRM-029, OM-017, OM-035)
12	- Returns data for the My Account returns view (CRM-088)
13	- Real-time stock availability:
14	  - Find in Boutique flyout and BOPIS boutique selection screen (CFD-043, CAI-038)
15	  - Collect in Boutique store + size validation (CAI-043)
16	  - Cart → checkout entry stock check (CAI-034 — this MuleSoft flow does not yet exist; the storefront falls back to the inventory feed until it is built)
17	- GiveX balance check (GC-037, GC-053) — MRT proxies an HTTPS request to MuleSoft, which owns the GiveX TCP connection and credentials
18	
19	Operations out of scope (server-to-server, outside the PWA layer):
20	
21	- SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore order creation and fulfilment writes
22	- SFCC ↔ MuleSoft ↔ Omneo customer / loyalty / address sync
23	- SFCC → MuleSoft → AP21 retail rewards balance lookup
24	- Product and pricing master feed AP21 → MuleSoft → SFCC (catalogue and pricebooks)
25	- The daily and 15-minute inventory feeds NewStore → MuleSoft → SFCC (CAI-019, CAI-020)
26	- Adyen fraud webhooks via MuleSoft (PAY-046)
27	- GiveX validate / redeem / refund (server-side via SCAPI/SFCC → NewStore adaptor → MuleSoft → GiveX)
28	- GiveX gift-card **issuance** at purchase (SCAPI/SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore → GiveX)
29	
30	## 2. PWA-layer architecture
31	
32	The flow below reflects the confirmed design from the MuleSoft integration PDFs (Jun 2025). MRT authenticates to MuleSoft using platform credentials (`client_id` + `client_secret`). The `customer_id` is passed as a plain UUID query parameter; MuleSoft does not verify shopper identity at the transport layer.
33	
34	```
35	Browser (My Account, cart, BOPIS flyout, etc.)
36	        │  Authenticated customer — customer_id known from SFCC session
37	        ▼
38	PWA fetches /mobify/proxy/mulesoft/<endpoint>
39	        │
40	        ▼
41	MRT Node layer:
42	   1. Reads customer_id from the authenticated SFCC session
43	   2. Appends client_id + client_secret as HTTP request headers (MRT environment variables)
44	   3. Forwards to https://mw.staging.zimmermann.com/magento-exp-api[-{env}]/<path>
45	      (env suffix: `-dev` for Dev, `-qa` for QA; no suffix for Prod — per vendor docs)
46	      with customer_id as a query parameter
47	        │
48	        ▼
49	MuleSoft (Magento Experience API):
50	   • Verifies channel auth via client_id + client_secret
51	   • Does NOT verify shopper identity at the transport layer
52	   • Routes internally to the Order Transactions Sync Process API → NewStore
53	        │
54	        ▼
55	NewStore response → MuleSoft → MRT → Browser (typed JSON, only the fields needed)
56	```
57	
58	- The browser never carries MuleSoft credentials. `client_id` and `client_secret` are held as MRT environment variables and are never exposed to the browser bundle.
59	- `customer_id` is a UUID string. MRT reads it from the authenticated SFCC session (step 1 above) — never from browser-supplied input. This prevents a browser from retrieving another customer's data by substituting a different UUID.
60	
61	## 3. Endpoint inventory
62	
63	Endpoints marked ✅ have confirmed paths and response schemas from the MuleSoft technical design documents. Endpoints marked ⏳ are working assumptions pending the formal OpenAPI specification (open item 1 in §9).
64	
65	| Endpoint | Status | Used by | Backed by | Requirement |
66	|---|---|---|---|---|
67	| `GET /api/orders?customer_id={…}&offset={…}&count={…}` | ✅ | Order history list (My Account) | NewStore | CRM-056, CRM-057, OM-035, RRC-013 |
68	| `GET /api/orders/{order_id}?id_type=internal` | ✅ | Order detail page | NewStore | CRM-071, CRM-072 |
69	| `GET /api/returns?customer_id={…}&offset={…}&count={…}` | ✅ | My Account returns view | NewStore Returns API | CRM-088, RRC-007 |
70	| `POST /api/find-in-store` body: `{ProductId, CountryCode}` | ✅ | Find in Boutique flyout + BOPIS screen | NewStore | CFD-043, CAI-038 |
71	| Orders list with `count=3` — confirm path with integration team | ⏳ | Account dashboard summary | NewStore | CRM-029 |
72	| GiveX balance check — path TBC; flows PWA → MRT → MuleSoft → GiveX (MuleSoft owns the GiveX TCP socket pool) | ⏳ | Gift card balance in My Account and at checkout | GiveX via MuleSoft | GC-037, GC-053 |
73	| Collect in Boutique validation — path TBC | ⏳ | Collect in Boutique store + size validation | NewStore | CAI-043 |
74	| Cart → checkout entry stock check — MuleSoft flow not yet built | ⏳ | Cart → checkout entry | NewStore | CAI-034 |
75	
76	The full OpenAPI specification is open item 1 in §9.
77	
78	## 4. Authentication and credentials
79	
80	| Credential | Where used | Sensitivity |
81	|---|---|---|
82	| `client_id` | MRT environment variable; sent on every request to MuleSoft as an HTTP request header (never as a URL query parameter) | Secret — never reaches the browser |
83	| `client_secret` | MRT environment variable; sent on every request to MuleSoft as an HTTP request header (never as a URL query parameter) | Secret — never reaches the browser |
84	| `customer_id` (UUID) | Plain query parameter on orders / returns calls; read from the SFCC session server-side | Not a secret — MRT enforces it matches the authenticated session |
85	
86	One `client_id` / `client_secret` pair per environment. Credential rotation is owned by the integration team.
87	
88	## 5. Data exchanged

# 03 — MuleSoft (PWA-direct reads via MRT proxy)

## 1. Purpose and scope

MuleSoft is the integration middleware that sits between SFCC and Zimmermann's back-office systems (NewStore OMS, AP21, Omneo, Narvar). The vast majority of MuleSoft traffic is server-to-server from SFCC and is out of scope here. This document covers the **separate, direct path** in which the PWA's Managed Runtime Node layer calls MuleSoft directly via `/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...` for a small set of read operations where SFCC adds no value to the round-trip.

Operations in scope of this document (PWA → MRT → MuleSoft, with SFCC outside the read path):

- Order history list (CRM-056 / CRM-057, RRC-013) — the 50 most recent orders, online and in-store
- Order detail (CRM-071 / CRM-072)
- Account dashboard "recent orders" summary (CRM-029, OM-017, OM-035)
- Returns data for the My Account returns view (CRM-088)
- Real-time stock availability:
  - Find in Boutique flyout and BOPIS boutique selection screen (CFD-043, CAI-038)
  - Collect in Boutique store + size validation (CAI-043)
  - Cart → checkout entry stock check (CAI-034 — this MuleSoft flow does not yet exist; the storefront falls back to the inventory feed until it is built)
- GiveX balance check (GC-037, GC-053) — MRT proxies an HTTPS request to MuleSoft, which owns the GiveX TCP connection and credentials

Operations out of scope (server-to-server, outside the PWA layer):

- SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore order creation and fulfilment writes
- SFCC ↔ MuleSoft ↔ Omneo customer / loyalty / address sync
- SFCC → MuleSoft → AP21 retail rewards balance lookup
- Product and pricing master feed AP21 → MuleSoft → SFCC (catalogue and pricebooks)
- The daily and 15-minute inventory feeds NewStore → MuleSoft → SFCC (CAI-019, CAI-020)
- Adyen fraud webhooks via MuleSoft (PAY-046)
- GiveX validate / redeem / refund (server-side via SCAPI/SFCC → NewStore adaptor → MuleSoft → GiveX)
- GiveX gift-card **issuance** at purchase (SCAPI/SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore → GiveX)

## 2. PWA-layer architecture

The flow below reflects the confirmed design from the MuleSoft integration PDFs (Jun 2025). MRT authenticates to MuleSoft using platform credentials (`client_id` + `client_secret`). The `customer_id` is passed as a plain UUID query parameter; MuleSoft does not verify shopper identity at the transport layer.

```
Browser (My Account, cart, BOPIS flyout, etc.)
        │  Authenticated customer — customer_id known from SFCC session
        ▼
PWA fetches /mobify/proxy/mulesoft/<endpoint>
        │
        ▼
MRT Node layer:
   1. Reads customer_id from the authenticated SFCC session
   2. Appends client_id + client_secret as HTTP request headers (MRT environment variables)
   3. Forwards to https://mw.staging.zimmermann.com/magento-exp-api[-{env}]/<path>
      (env suffix: `-dev` for Dev, `-qa` for QA; no suffix for Prod — per vendor docs)
      with customer_id as a query parameter
        │
        ▼
MuleSoft (Magento Experience API):
   • Verifies channel auth via client_id + client_secret
   • Does NOT verify shopper identity at the transport layer
   • Routes internally to the Order Transactions Sync Process API → NewStore
        │
        ▼
NewStore response → MuleSoft → MRT → Browser (typed JSON, only the fields needed)
```

- The browser never carries MuleSoft credentials. `client_id` and `client_secret` are held as MRT environment variables and are never exposed to the browser bundle.
- `customer_id` is a UUID string. MRT reads it from the authenticated SFCC session (step 1 above) — never from browser-supplied input. This prevents a browser from retrieving another customer's data by substituting a different UUID.

## 3. Endpoint inventory

Endpoints marked ✅ have confirmed paths and response schemas from the MuleSoft technical design documents. Endpoints marked ⏳ are working assumptions pending the formal OpenAPI specification (open item 1 in §9).

| Endpoint | Status | Used by | Backed by | Requirement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/orders?customer_id={…}&offset={…}&count={…}` | ✅ | Order history list (My Account) | NewStore | CRM-056, CRM-057, OM-035, RRC-013 |
| `GET /api/orders/{order_id}?id_type=internal` | ✅ | Order detail page | NewStore | CRM-071, CRM-072 |
| `GET /api/returns?customer_id={…}&offset={…}&count={…}` | ✅ | My Account returns view | NewStore Returns API | CRM-088, RRC-007 |
| `POST /api/find-in-store` body: `{ProductId, CountryCode}` | ✅ | Find in Boutique flyout + BOPIS screen | NewStore | CFD-043, CAI-038 |
| Orders list with `count=3` — confirm path with integration team | ⏳ | Account dashboard summary | NewStore | CRM-029 |
| GiveX balance check — path TBC; flows PWA → MRT → MuleSoft → GiveX (MuleSoft owns the GiveX TCP socket pool) | ⏳ | Gift card balance in My Account and at checkout | GiveX via MuleSoft | GC-037, GC-053 |
| Collect in Boutique validation — path TBC | ⏳ | Collect in Boutique store + size validation | NewStore | CAI-043 |
| Cart → checkout entry stock check — MuleSoft flow not yet built | ⏳ | Cart → checkout entry | NewStore | CAI-034 |

The full OpenAPI specification is open item 1 in §9.

## 4. Authentication and credentials

| Credential | Where used | Sensitivity |
|---|---|---|
| `client_id` | MRT environment variable; sent on every request to MuleSoft as an HTTP request header (never as a URL query parameter) | Secret — never reaches the browser |
| `client_secret` | MRT environment variable; sent on every request to MuleSoft as an HTTP request header (never as a URL query parameter) | Secret — never reaches the browser |
| `customer_id` (UUID) | Plain query parameter on orders / returns calls; read from the SFCC session server-side | Not a secret — MRT enforces it matches the authenticated session |

One `client_id` / `client_secret` pair per environment. Credential rotation is owned by the integration team.

## 5. Data exchanged

| Direction | Data | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Browser → MRT | Authenticated customer session (customer_id extracted server-side); endpoint path; small query/body payload where applicable | The browser never sees MuleSoft credentials. |
| MRT → MuleSoft | `client_id` + `client_secret` (channel auth); `customer_id` as a query parameter; endpoint payload | `client_id`/`client_secret` authorise the channel. MuleSoft does not verify shopper identity at the transport layer. |
| MuleSoft → MRT → Browser | Typed JSON — order summary, order detail, boutique stock list, returns list | MRT projects only the fields the UI consumes to keep payload small. |

No PII flows back to the browser beyond what the customer already owns (their own order data, their own returns). Boutique stock responses contain no PII.

## 6. Performance and loading strategy

- All MuleSoft reads are made only when the relevant route or interaction triggers them. The order-history list does not preload on home; the boutique inventory call only fires when the Find in Boutique flyout opens (CAI-038).
- The MuleSoft vendor response time target (per the received PDFs) is < 2.5 s. The PWA's own soft-failure threshold of 2 s (see §7) is intentionally stricter.
- Working performance budget (working assumption — pending SLA confirmation with the integration team): p95 under 800 ms for order list and order detail; under 500 ms for boutique inventory checks.
- TanStack Query caches order list and order detail responses on the client; stale data is acceptable for the dashboard summary and order list but never for cart → checkout entry stock checks, which always re-fetch.
- `<link rel="preconnect">` to the MuleSoft host is emitted from the My Account entry routes once the customer is authenticated.

## 7. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| MuleSoft rejects channel auth (invalid `client_id`/`client_secret`) | Return 401 to the browser. This indicates a misconfigured or rotated credential — requires an ops fix, not a user retry. Surface a generic error UI. |
| MuleSoft 5xx on order list | Order history view shows an explicit retry UI. The contract is "explicit retry, never partial data". |
| MuleSoft 5xx on cart → checkout entry stock check (CAI-034) | Block checkout entry with a clear error. Do not silently progress; a stale stock decision risks an oversell. |
| MuleSoft 5xx on Find in Boutique inventory (CFD-043) | Show "Stock information temporarily unavailable" inside the flyout and a retry CTA. Do not fall back to cached data — boutique stock is real-time by design. |
| MuleSoft 5xx on Collect in Boutique validation (CAI-043) | Reject the boutique selection with an error; the shopper can pick a different store or method. |
| MuleSoft timeout above 2 seconds | Treated as a soft failure. UI degrades gracefully per the rows above. |
| NewStore upstream of MuleSoft is down | Surfaced to the storefront as a MuleSoft 5xx. Same handling. |

## 8. Security and privacy

- `client_id` and `client_secret` are held as MRT environment variables and never appear in browser JavaScript, request URLs, or client-accessible logs.
- All MRT → MuleSoft traffic is over TLS 1.2+.
- `customer_id` is a plain UUID query parameter passed to MuleSoft. MuleSoft does not verify shopper identity at the transport layer — MuleSoft trusts the channel. Impersonation is prevented at the MRT layer: MRT reads `customer_id` from the authenticated SFCC session only, never from browser-supplied input.
- No PII is logged at the MRT layer beyond a request ID and the endpoint name.

## 9. Open items requiring client confirmation

1. **MuleSoft OpenAPI specification.** MuleSoft to publish a versioned OpenAPI document covering every endpoint the storefront calls (order history and detail, returns, gift-card balance check, and any other MuleSoft-fronted endpoint in scope), including request and response schemas, error codes, and pagination contracts. The PDFs received (Jun 2025) provide sample schemas sufficient for initial implementation, but a formal versioned spec is still needed.
2. **Per-environment MuleSoft credentials.** MuleSoft to supply, per environment: `client_id`, `client_secret`, and MuleSoft host. Prod URLs for orders and returns are not yet provisioned (blank in the received PDFs). A staging Find In Store URL has been received (`https://mw.staging.zimmermann.com/magento-exp-api/api/find-in-store`); the production host is not yet confirmed.
3. **Response payload contracts for order detail and returns — mostly resolved.** Full sample schemas for order list, order detail, and returns were extracted from the Magento Experience Integration and Customer Order Transactions Sync PDFs (v3.0 / v2.0, Jun 2025) and are sufficient for initial implementation. Minor residual points to confirm with Tryzens: `channel.type` values for online orders (sample data only shows in-store); whether the returns endpoint supports `offset`/`count` pagination; the `shop.id` inconsistency between list (`"storefront-catalog-eu"`) and detail (`"ZIMMERMANN_LONDON_STORE"`) responses; the full set of `psp` values for online payment methods (sample shows `"cash"` and `"store_credit"` only).
